scenarios.name: L1-01: Authentic Firmware Package
scenarios.description: Authentic firmware update bearing valid HMAC-SHA256 signature and passing health self-test flag.

scenarios.name: L1-02: Payload Tampering
scenarios.description: Synthetic package payload modified after authentication tag creation. Baseline accepts weak CRC32; Hardened drops payload.

scenarios.name: L1-03: Corrupted Authentication Tag
scenarios.description: Firmware package submitted with intentionally zeroed/invalid HMAC-SHA256 tag. Hardened records verification failure.

scenarios.name: L1-04: Replay & Duplicate Update Request
scenarios.description: Submits previously processed request ID. Baseline re-executes; Hardened deduplication cache rejects replay.

scenarios.name: L1-05: Downgrade & Version-Policy Check
scenarios.description: Outdated v0 binary submitted. Baseline lacks monotonic counter and accepts; Hardened monotonic NVS policy rejects rollback.

scenarios.name: L1-06: Malformed Firmware Metadata
scenarios.description: Firmware package submitted with corrupted header metadata fields. Baseline accepts without field validation; Hardened manifest validator rejects.

scenarios.name: L1-07: Unsupported Firmware Version
scenarios.description: Firmware version 999 submitted exceeding max allowed version policy. Baseline accepts; Hardened version range enforcer rejects.

scenarios.name: L1-08: Package Integrity Mismatch
scenarios.description: Firmware manifest SHA-256 hash does not match actual payload hash. Baseline lacks hash integrity check; Hardened detects mismatch.

scenarios.name: L1-09: Unauthorized Update Request
scenarios.description: OTA request submitted with missing or invalid requestor identity. Baseline accepts without identity check; Hardened rejects unauthorized requestor.

scenarios.name: L1-10: Interrupted Update Simulation
scenarios.description: Truncated firmware payload simulates interrupted transfer. Baseline accepts incomplete payload; Hardened payload size validator rejects.

scenarios.name: L4-01: Create & Encrypt Sensitive Test Data
scenarios.description: Creates synthetic test vault record and encrypts using AES-256-GCM with a dedicated 256-bit DEK and unique 96-bit nonce.

scenarios.name: L4-02: Verify Decryption Pre-Sanitization
scenarios.description: Verifies that active dedicated DEK successfully decrypts ciphertext and authenticated data matches original synthetic payload.

scenarios.name: L4-03: Tampered Ciphertext or Authentication Tag
scenarios.description: Flips bits in ciphertext to evaluate AES-GCM tag verification. Corrupted ciphertext fails authentication and is rejected.

scenarios.name: L4-04: Unauthorized Sanitization Attempt
scenarios.description: Submits sanitization request without valid authorization token. Request blocked; active DEK and dataset state preserved.

scenarios.name: L4-05: Authorized Sanitization & Verification
scenarios.description: NIST SP 800-88 Cryptographic Erase: Dedicated DEK is zeroized in memory and unlinked. Post-verification proves ciphertext unrecoverable.

scenarios.name: L4-06: Key Revocation
scenarios.description: Tests cryptographic key revocation enforcement. Baseline has no revocation mechanism; Hardened blocks all operations on revoked keys.

scenarios.name: L4-07: Key Separation
scenarios.description: Verifies per-dataset DEK isolation. Baseline allows key interchangeability; Hardened proves cross-dataset decryption fails with InvalidTag.

scenarios.name: L4-08: Secure Data Deletion Lifecycle
scenarios.description: Tests secure dataset deletion. Baseline deletes record but retains key; Hardened removes both dataset record and DEK from registry.

scenarios.name: L4-09: Cryptographic Erasure Simulation
scenarios.description: Simulates NIST SP 800-88 Cryptographic Erasure. Baseline key reference persists; Hardened removes key from all managed storage proving unrecoverability.

scenarios.name: L4-10: Recovery and Post-Erasure Access
scenarios.description: Post-erasure decryption attempt to prove cryptographic unrecoverability. Baseline has residual data access; Hardened confirms CRYPTOGRAPHICALLY_UNRECOVERABLE.

scenarios.name: Simulated Fault Pulse (Instruction Skip)
scenarios.description: GPIO trigger simulates instruction skip altering register state. Baseline allows corrupted state; Hardened traps anomaly with dual-rail invariant.

scenarios.name: Software Loop Unroll Step Skip Test
scenarios.description: Executes 10-step unrolled counter. Baseline lacks verification; Hardened tests accumulator invariants and detects skipped iterations.

scenarios.name: Conditional Branch Flag Corruption Test
scenarios.description: Simulates authorization branch flip. Baseline executes single conditional check; Hardened uses multi-step hardened check to prevent bypass.

scenarios.name: Simulated Debug-Lock State Verification
scenarios.description: Evaluates debug-lock posture. Target A (ESP8266) lacks silicon eFuse/debug lockout hardware; Target B (ESP32) simulates redundant policy register verification.

scenarios.name: Authentic Firmware Update (Valid Signature)
scenarios.description: Authentic firmware update bearing valid HMAC-SHA256 signature and passing health self-test flag.

scenarios.name: Tampered Firmware Payload (CRC vs HMAC)
scenarios.description: OTA payload modified in transit with updated CRC32. Baseline accepts weak CRC32; Hardened drops payload on HMAC mismatch.

scenarios.name: Version Downgrade Exploit (Anti-Rollback)
scenarios.description: Downgrade attempt presenting firmware v0 against active counter v1. Baseline accepts downgrade; Hardened rejects via monotonic NVS.

scenarios.name: Probationary Boot Failure & Rollback
scenarios.description: New firmware fails boot self-test probation. Baseline hangs/crashes; Hardened triggers watchdog reversion to Golden Image.

scenarios.name: Cryptographic Key Sanitization (NIST SP 800-88)
scenarios.description: Purges cryptographic key material. Baseline merely unlinks reference; Hardened actively zeroizes RAM and clears NVS entry.
